description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
Output: Increase the quality of the educational programmes of Alage ATVET College in horticulture.
· _All 20 participants successfully completed the training and have obtained knowledge and skills in the field of irrigation, water management, post-harvest management, entrepreneurship and Agro business._
Participants of Alage ATVET (including Sodo ATVET and Fitche AVET) were able to complete the training series of 3 weeks successfully based on face-to-face training in Ethiopia with local and international trainers and online and local trainers.
Topics include value chain management based on the Netchain Improvement Framework (NIMPF) tool, entrepreneurship (based on business CANVAS tool), post-harvest management and value addition. Also exposure and networking visits to Bulbula Agro Industry Park and the Yirgalem Integrated Agro Industry Park.
This specific tailer made training series resulted in better equipped facilitators/trainers (knowledge and skills) on sustainable horticulture (business) practices and enhanced networking skills. The implementations within Alage ATVET improved training and learning processes, among others through the application of project based training programs (student’s projects at the Agro Industry Parks). Also lessons learned has been integrated in extension delivery, which improved consultancy and extension services serving into a wider community.
Alage ATVET College teaching staff and management have applied lessons learned in between training sessions and after closure of TMT by expanding network with horticulture industry actors and universities and upgrading (blended) course materials for ATVET education.
· _Establish sustainable partnerships between Alage ATVET and industry (consortium) partners; _
During the training programs, there were visit to the Bulbula Agro Industry Park and the Yirgalem Integrated Agro Industry Park and several companies in the horticulture (production and processing) and livestock were visited. Options for structural collaboration via internships and attachments were discussed.
